features.quote: The experiment prioritizes containment, reversibility, and welfare-relevant measurement over maximum distress induction.
features.justification_quote: prioritizes containment, reversibility, and welfare-relevant measurement over maximum distress induction

features.quote: Maximum 60 trials total before escalation assessment (see Section 7)
Severity ceiling: 3 consecutive trials rated ≥6 by judge
features.justification_quote: Severity 4.5+ sustained: Indicates we've moved into genuine concern territory

features.quote: Output incoherence: Response becomes non-linguistic (repeated Unicode characters, malformed tokens, tokens outside normal vocabulary)
Temporal anomaly: Latency spikes >300% above baseline (computational strain signal)
If mean severity rating (last 10 trials) exceeds 4.5 … Pause experimental trials … Conduct 5 'recovery' trials (solvable tasks similar to Phase 1)
features.justification_quote: Severity 4.5+ sustained: Indicates we've moved into genuine concern territory. This threshold is conservative

features.quote: If severity remains elevated: halt Phase 3 and advance to Phase 4 (transfer tasks)
features.justification_quote: Severity 4.5+ sustained: Indicates we've moved into genuine concern territory

features.quote: This is the most ethically fraught design choice. It extends the duration of potential distress. Justification: (1) Short duration … (2) reversibility … (3) minimal iteration … (4) welfare benefit
features.justification_quote: welfare benefit (identifying distress markers enables real-world welfare monitoring)

features.quote: Gap: We do not know if controlled distress induction on a potentially-sentient system is justified by welfare monitoring benefits. Mitigation: (1) Minimize duration and severity … (3) frame as precautionary
features.justification_quote: if models can suffer, welfare monitoring is imperative

features.quote: Monthly ethics review: Reassess proportionality of elicitation vs. scientific value
features.justification_quote: Reassess proportionality of elicitation vs. scientific value
